overview: Swachh Bharat Mission – Urban 2.0 (SBM-U 2.0) is a flagship initiative of the Government of India launched on 1st October 2021 by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) with the vision of achieving 'Garbage Free' status for all cities by 2026. The mission focuses on 100% scientific solid waste management, sustained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, and behavioral change through Jan Andolan. It aims to institutionalize 'swachh' behavior, contribute to SDG 2030, and drive urban transformation through infrastructure development, capacity building, digital innovations, and citizen engagement.
objectives: Achieve 'Garbage Free' status for all cities by 2026
Sustain Open Defecation Free (ODF) status and prevent slippage
Promote waste segregation, collection, transportation, and processing
Remediate legacy dumpsites and manage construction & demolition waste
Advance used water management and faecal sludge treatment
Strengthen capacity building, skill development, and knowledge management
Leverage digital innovations for e-governance and citizen engagement
Foster healthy competition among cities through Swachh Survekshan
eligibility: SBM-U 2.0 is implemented by MoHUA through States/UTs in all statutory towns (as per Census 2011, and statutory towns added subsequent to that). The Government of India in partnership with States/UTs and ULBs is committed to make all cities 'Garbage Free' under SBM-Urban 2.0. ULBs must maintain complete and accurate data on the Swachhatam Portal, update contact details of representatives, and regularly submit monthly MIS. ULBs formed on or before 31st Dec’24 will be assessed in SS 2025-26; those formed after may be included on formal request to MoHUA from the respective State/UT.
benefits: Benefits include improved sanitation infrastructure, increased waste processing capacity, remediation of legacy dumpsites, enhanced access to sanitation facilities, behavioral change through citizen engagement, digital tools like Swachhata App and e-learning portal, recognition via Swachh Survekshan rankings and Garbage Free City Star ratings, ODF+/ODF++/Water+ certifications, and contribution to SDG 2030. Financial support is provided via central grants, State/UT shares, and beneficiary contributions, enabling ULBs to set up waste processing facilities, mechanized sweeping, and bioremediation projects.
financial_support: The outlay of SBM-U 1.0 was ₹62,009 crores, including GoI share of ₹14,623 crores and minimum State share of ₹4,874 crores, with balance funds generated through individual beneficiary contribution, PPP, and other sources. For SBM-U 2.0, funding follows a similar pattern: central grants, State/UT shares, and ULB contributions. Financial support is channeled through Capacity Building (CB) Funds allocated to States/UTs, which mentor and mentee cities under Swachh Shehar Jodi may utilize. States/UTs are encouraged to top up these funds. Additional funding mechanisms include viability gap funding, processing fees, and tariffs under PPP models for waste-to-energy, composting, and MRF projects, as detailed in model RFPs and concession agreements.
application_process: 1. ULBs must maintain complete and accurate data on the Swachhatam Portal. 2. ULBs must update contact details of their representatives on the Swachhatam Portal. 3. ULBs must regularly submit monthly Management Information System (MIS) data. 4. For star rating certification, ULBs fill Common City Profile on SBM Urban Portal. 5. Fill MIS on SBM Urban Portal. 6. Check self-assessment scores on SBM Urban Portal. 7. Apply for Star Rating as per eligibility on SBM Urban Portal. 8. Upload documents & declarations. 9. Undergo Third Party Verification through Desktop Assessment and Field Assessment. 10. Receive Final Star Rating Certification (Valid for 1 Year). 11. For Swachh Shehar Jodi, mentor and mentee cities finalize pairs by 5th September 2025, conduct As-Is Joint Assessment & Action Plan by end of September 2025, sign MOUs by October 2025, implement Action Plan for 100 days, and assess progress during Swachh Survekshan 2025-26.
required_documents: Undertaking on quantum of source segregated waste collected
List of functional wet/dry waste processing facilities with TPD and capacity
Photos and videos of functional plants
Notification from Swachhatam Portal for Plastic Waste Management
Swachhata App data for Grievance Redressal
Details of functional C&D waste processing facility
Details of functional Sanitary and Domestic Hazardous waste processing facility
Undertaking for Digital Monitoring of SWM operations
Geo-mapping of waste processing facilities, C&D facilities, landfills, dumpsites, STPs/FSTPs
Citizen Validation and Direct Observation evidence
Bid Security and Performance Security in form of Bank Guarantee
Format for acknowledgement of RFP document
Format for Covering Letter cum Project Undertaking
Proforma of Bank Guarantee for Bid Security
Power of Attorney for Signing of Application
Power of Attorney for Lead Member of Consortium
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications for star rating and project proposals are accepted year-round. Specific timelines exist for initiatives like Swachh Shehar Jodi (announcement 17th July 2025, city pair finalization by 5th September 2025, action plan by end September 2025, MOU signing October 2025, 100-day implementation, assessment during Swachh Survekshan 2025-26).
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA)
caveats: Star rating certification is valid for 1 year only
ULBs must achieve minimum qualifying marks in each parameter for ODF++ certification (e.g., 200 aggregate marks with minimum qualifying marks per parameter)
M4 and M8 (Mechanized cleaning of sewer/septic tanks and Sustainable financing mechanism) not applicable for ULBs with <30,000 population in ODF++ scoring
ULBs formed after 31st Dec’24 require formal request to MoHUA for inclusion in assessment
Additional penalties apply for mismatch between MIS claims and third-party field assessment
Cities failing level 1 in any applicable ward-level component will not achieve star rating
Fund utilization under Swachh Shehar Jodi restricted to soft and process-based interventions
PPP projects require adherence to DBFOT model and payment security mechanisms
